subject: Day 16: cluster feeding likely tonight; supply calibration
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 16. The growth spurt is likely peaking. Evening cluster feeding can run for hours; if breastfeeding, this is the demand signal that drives supply up over the next 48-72 hours. It resolves on its own.

Action items
- Plan a low-commitment evening; cluster feeding is easier to ride out when nothing else is scheduled.
- If supplementing, offer the breast first and top off after, to preserve the supply signal.
- Confirm the EPDS is done and acted on if the score was elevated. Postpartum Support International: https://www.postpartum.net/
- Continue the daycare or nanny shortlist; tours and waitlist deposits take weeks to arrange. Care.com: https://www.care.com/
- Keep the feeding log current.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Hours of evening cluster feeding; fussiness that settles with holding.
- [low concern] Baby acne peaking; cord site fully healed for most infants by now.
- [monitor] Signs that cluster feeding is not transferring milk — fewer than six wet diapers, no settling at all between feeds.
- [call within 24h] Forceful projectile vomiting with weight stagnation. Persistent inability to console paired with back-arching during feeds.
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C). Lethargy, refusing all feeds, blue or grey color, breathing faster than 60 per minute at rest, persistent grunting, projectile or bilious-green vomiting. Call 911 for blue lips or unresponsiveness!

Enrichment opportunities
- Fit tummy time into the calmer parts of the day; 15 minutes total across short bouts. AAP HealthyChildren on tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Use skin-to-skin contact during cluster feeding; it calms both of you and supports milk transfer.
- Take conversational turns with his coos during awake-alert windows. Romeo et al., Psych Science 2018: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/
- Give him a slow-moving high-contrast target to track when he is calm and alert.

Upcoming
- Day 17-21: growth spurt resolving; feeding returns to its prior cadence.
- Day 28-35: 1-month well visit; first social smiles.
- Day 35-42: peak crying curve approaches.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Calms when picked up or spoken to
  AAP window: day 14-60
  What to look for: Early co-regulation. Not the same as stopping crying immediately — look for any shift in state.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/calms-with-soothing/complete

- Briefly lifts head during tummy time
  AAP window: day 14-60
  What to look for: Few seconds of head lift, even with bobble, counts. Builds neck strength for later head control.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/brief-head-lift/complete

- Quiets or turns toward a familiar voice
  AAP window: day 7-45
  What to look for: Voice recognition begins before birth; postnatally it shows as orienting or settling to a parent's voice.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-1-Month.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/recognizes-parent-voice/complete

- Watches your face when you talk
  AAP window: day 7-60
  What to look for: Baseline social orientation. Look for sustained gaze, even briefly, during alert windows.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/tracks-face-briefly/complete

- Moves both arms and both legs
  AAP window: day 0-60
  What to look for: Symmetric, spontaneous movement of all four limbs. Asymmetry warrants pediatric attention.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/moves-arms-and-legs/complete
